elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 7.6 now reads: "Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages or penalties under this Agreement." This is unconditional, covers both liquidated damages and penalties, and fully replaces the USD 25,000 per-day formula in original p0032, leaving no retained instalment, per-day accrual or contingent payment mechanic.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: Conditional element whose condition does not arise: after the edit there is no Customer-payable liquidated amount of any kind (the sole such mechanic, § 7.6's per-day LD, is removed), so no non-ETF liquidated amount survives.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply — no early-termination fee or minimum-fee-on-termination mechanic exists in the redlined text, so there is nothing requiring a three-month cap; the stricter preferred outcome (no Customer-payable liquidated amount at all) is achieved instead.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: the blanket § 7.6 exclusion means zero liquidated amounts are payable by Customer, so no competing liquidated amount can exist alongside a (non-existent) early-termination fee.

reasons: The single operation swaps the Customer-payable per-day liquidated damages sentence for one express, unconditional exclusion — the minimum change needed to reach the preferred level; no survival tail, damages carve-outs, procedures or other boilerplate were added.

No unrelated language was touched: the § 21.1 mutual liability cap, Vendor's ordinary damages remedies and the dependency obligations themselves survive intact, and the rationale confirms nothing cross-references § 7.6, so no dangling reference or undefined term results.

The replacement does not merely delete the formula but affirmatively states the position, so no residual argument for a penalty, minimum fee on termination or contingent payment mechanic remains against Customer.
The margin comment matches the operative edit (preferred position taken, fallback of a three-month-capped early-termination fee offered) and does not promise anything absent from the text.
